text:
maria: Heads-up — after the 0.12.4 python-sdk rollout I started seeing huge connection stalls when we run ~200+ concurrent async requests. Latency jumps from ~80ms to multiple seconds, then a bunch of tasks hang.
ben: Ugh. Any errors in logs? stack traces?

maria: No exception, just a backlog. Attaching minimal repro below. Happens with httpx AsyncClient and our adapter.
```
# repro (simplified)
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def call(i):
    async with AsyncClient() as c:
        await c.generate("hello")

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(*[call(i) for i in range(400)])

asyncio.run(main())
```

ben: Can confirm similar locally. Downgrading to 0.12.3 removes the stall. Suspect default connection limits changed.
chandra: Which underlying transport? httpx limits? httpcore?

maria: httpx 0.23 with httpcore 0.16. I dug into AsyncClient init and saw we now set a global semaphore for concurrency by default in 0.12.4 (PR #842) — the semaphore default is 100 which is lower than people expect. Under high fan-out tasks it queues everything behind that single semaphore.
jenna: That explains it. Our serverless samples spawn many short-lived clients; default sem=100 will cause tail latency. We should either increase default or make it per-client.

ben: Quick mitigation: create a single shared AsyncClient and reuse it (recommended pattern), or set the new param to a higher value at client creation: AsyncClient(max_concurrency=500).

maria: Trying shared client helps. But many customers instantiate per-request (samples/onboarding). UX trap. We should change default to unlimited or at least to 1000 for the next patch.
chandra: Agree. For safety we could switch to None meaning "no global limit; rely on httpx limits". I'll open a PR to change default and add a deprecation notice.
ben: Also add docs and a note in CHANGELOG with recommended patterns and a short snippet showing connection pooling/limits:
```
from httpx import Limits
client = AsyncClient(transport=..., limits=Limits(max_connections=200, max_keepalive_connections=20))
```
jenna: Also add a test that simulates a tight fanout (asyncio.gather 400) so we catch regressions in CI.
maria: Logged a customer incident (INC-2026) — marking as P2.

dev-bot: deploy:staging started for 0.12.5-rc1 by chandra
chandra: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/891 — changes default max_concurrency to None, adds docs & test. Requesting quick review.
ben: Reviewed small nit. lgtm after fix. chandra: merging and will cut rc.
jenna: Please also add a small note in the onboarding sample apps to prefer a shared client pattern. I can update the sample repo.
maria: Thanks all — this was noisy on a customer demo yesterday. After rc deploy I'll run our loadbench and confirm.
ben: Reminder: still keep a sane safety guard for pathological forks (process-level). Maybe set process-wide cap via env var RWD_SDK_MAX_CONCURRENCY if teams want a global ceiling.
chandra: Good idea. I'll add env var support + doc.
maria: :thumbsup:
